solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old French bread

parts.note: bread is slang for money, so this means the former currency of the French, replaced by the euro, not a baguette

explanation.surface: A request at the bakery for a stale baguette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' looks like a loaf, but it is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the national currency of France until the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: A way around isle that's passable

indicators.note: around means the first piece encircles the second

parts.note: far means a long way, as in 'far off'
I is the standard abbreviation for isle or island

explanation.surface: A road that circles an island and is just about good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair work is adequate but not outstanding, the same middling sense as passable.

clue.text: Skinny doctor's first aid kit?

parts.note: a very thin person is called this, and a doctor's medical bag might whimsically be imagined as holding bones

explanation.surface: A thin GP's medical bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone extremely thin, all skeleton and no flesh.

clue.text: Wound up Conservative gets lubricated

parts.note: oiled means lubricated, and also slangily drunk

explanation.surface: A Tory politician who has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound up' reads as agitated, but here it is the past of wind, as a spring is wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or spring that has been wound up is coiled into loops.

clue.text: Girl at bar plays rock here?

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters move about freely, signalling they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl at a bar plays rock music in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' reads as music; it is the Rock, the British territory's famous limestone headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibraltar is known as the Rock, after the great limestone outcrop that dominates it.

clue.text: Grandee in ridiculous syrup

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests something absurdly out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman made to look silly while dipped in syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a sweet red cordial made from pomegranate, used in cocktails.

clue.text: Film graduate on motorway touring Britain

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the road's letters surround the other piece

parts.note: M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A graduate on a road trip round Britain by motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is England's first major motorway, its 1 standing in as I; 'on' places the graduate above it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi is the 1942 Disney animated feature about a young deer.

clue.text: A bishop shot up by soldier with a big head?

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a shot is a go, an attempt
a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so ant stands in for soldier

explanation.surface: A bishop shot by a soldier, the soldier being conceited.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a big head is conceited, the figurative sense of an inflated ego.

clue.text: Needleworker's work is tasteless stuff

definitions.meaning: to make tatting, a lace done with a shuttle and thread

explanation.surface: A sniffy verdict that someone's embroidery is in poor taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatting is handmade knotted lace; tat is also British slang for cheap, vulgar junk.

clue.text: Basic training needed for adult miner

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: An adult miner needs only elementary training.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudimental is a variant of rudimentary: elementary, at the first stage.

clue.text: Fancy Slormgorm's a spirit with energy

parts.note: the setter's name stands for 'I', so Slormgorm's is I'm
gin is a spirit
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of being a lively spirit, or invites us to picture it.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves by name: Slormgorm's means 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as a verb is to suppose or picture something in the mind.

clue.text: Drop of Malbec flipping weary editor deserved

indicators.note: a drop of a wine is a tiny amount, here just its opening letter
flipping means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to tire is to weary

explanation.surface: A tired editor earned a little red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive, but it turns TIRE into ERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: What has been merited has been earned, the same sense as deserved.

clue.text: US theatre I promote or nag about

indicators.note: about means all around, so the letters are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor or producer promotes a play or nags others about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests the stage; it is the medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a hospital's surgery room an operating room, Britons an operating theatre.

clue.text: I'll supply you with contacts at work

definitions.text: I'll supply you with contacts at work

parts.words: I'll supply you with contacts at work
parts.note: reads as a networker offering business connections, but the contacts are contact lenses fitted by an eye professional

explanation.surface: A networker offering useful business connections.
explanation.definitionFit: An optometrist tests eyesight and prescribes contact lenses as well as glasses.

clue.text: Those ticked off by inspection on Rolls

parts.note: a check is an inspection
rolls are lists, as in electoral rolls

explanation.surface: People told off after an inspection of their Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ticked off' reads as scolded; here it means items marked with a tick. 'On' places the inspection above the rolls in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Checklists are lists of items each marked with a tick once done.

clue.text: Husband loves pinching bishop's bum

indicators.note: pinching means squeezing between, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O, so loves gives two Os
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cheeky husband grabbing a bishop's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' reads as backside; it is the American sense of a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A bum in American slang is a vagrant or tramp, and a hobo is a wandering homeless person.

clue.text: Criminal losing it by north London borough

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook losing his temper in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Islington is a borough of inner north London.

clue.text: Literature one software mogul contests in court

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Bill Gates founded Microsoft

explanation.surface: A tech billionaire takes a literary dispute to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To litigate is to take a dispute to law, fighting it before a judge.

clue.text: Loch overlooked by resort has pleasant quality

indicators.note: in a down clue, being overlooked by puts the second piece below the first

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake, so Ness stands for the loch

explanation.surface: A Scottish lake seen from above by a holiday town is pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceness is the state of being agreeable, a noun for a pleasant nature.

clue.text: Tory stupid to get NHS department in pickle?

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a Tory
dim means stupid
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department in Britain's National Health Service

explanation.surface: A dim Tory getting the health service into a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' reads as a predicament; it is the relish, an example of a condiment, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickle is a relish served with food, one example of a condiment.

clue.text: Woman finally made two grand? Ace!

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a grand, so two grand is MM
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A woman eventually earned two thousand, which is great.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a female first name, as in Jane Austen's heroine.

clue.text: Prisoner must get dog…agree?

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Should a prisoner be allowed a dog, do you agree?
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion, a formal word for agree.

clue.text: Isn't Pole struggling with Sting LP?

indicators.note: struggling suggests a tangle of movement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Polish fan who cannot cope with a Sting album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'LP' reads as a record album, but it is the military abbreviation for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: LP is a standard military abbreviation for a forward observation spot used to eavesdrop on the enemy.

clue.text: Congressional results matter

definitions.meaning: congress is an old word for sex, and ... means offspring, its results

explanation.surface: Political outcomes in Washington are what count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congressional' reads as the US legislature; it is sexual congress.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means children or descendants, and also a topic or point in question.

clue.text: You old? That's awful, right?

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
ah is an exclamation of dismay

explanation.surface: Someone tactlessly asks whether you are old and then agrees it is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the sarcastic 'yeah, right', with 'right?' meaning yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeah is casual for yes, the affirmative reply that 'right' can also express.

clue.text: People who flog old comic actor

definitions.meaning: people who flog, or sell, goods
Peter ... was the British comic actor of The Pink Panther films

explanation.surface: Market traders who once sold an elderly comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' is British slang for sell, not beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sellers are vendors; Peter Sellers (1925-1980) starred as Inspector Clouseau.

clue.text: One after the heart of Alex Garland

indicators.note: in this down clue, after means the next piece comes later in the answer
the heart of a word is its central part, here its middle two letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone pursues the affections of the film director Alex Garland.
explanation.walkthrough: Alex Garland is a novelist and director, but the surname is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck.

clue.text: Touchy jazz fan upset one roofer laid

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
a tile is one of the items a roofer lays

explanation.surface: A sensitive jazz lover upset by a roofer's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touchy' reads as irritable; it means relating to touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile describes things perceived by or relating to the sense of touch.

clue.text: Old maids in DJs, might one say?

definitions.text: Old maids in DJs, might one say?

parts.words: Old maids in DJs, might one say?
parts.note: disc jockeys spin records, so whimsically they could be called by the word for unmarried women

explanation.surface: Elderly unmarried women dressed in dinner jackets.
explanation.walkthrough: DJs reads as dinner jackets, but it is disc jockeys, who spin records.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinsters is a dated term for unmarried women, traditionally old maids.

clue.text: Gag poor fellow in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means the word is as heard rather than written

parts.note: a wretch is an unfortunate person

explanation.surface: Silencing an unfortunate man during a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' reads as silencing; it means to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to choke or heave as if about to vomit, which is to retch.
